fields.label: Match Threshold
fields.description: How similar two faces must be, from 0 to 1, to count as the same person. Higher is stricter: fewer wrong people accepted, but more genuine employees rejected. Start around 0.5 and adjust from the Face Verification Log. Applies to every phone and kiosk within a minute.

fields.label: Embedding Model
fields.description: Identifier of the face-recognition model the app uses to turn a face into numbers. Face Templates made with a different model cannot be compared, so the server refuses them. Change it only when you roll out a new model and re-register faces.

fields.label: Challenge Lifetime (seconds)
fields.description: How long a one-time code issued to a phone stays valid. The phone must send its check-in before it expires; each code works only once, which blocks replayed requests. Raise it only if slow networks cause timeouts.

fields.label: Failed Attempts Before Lockout
fields.description: Consecutive failed face or PIN checks for one employee before that employee is locked out. Face and PIN failures count together. A successful check resets the count.

fields.label: Lockout Minutes
fields.description: How long a locked-out employee must wait before trying again with face or PIN.

fields.label: Require HR Approval Of New Faces
fields.description: When on, a new face stays pending until HR approves it. Leave it on if employees can register their own face, so nobody enrols another person's face under their own account.

fields.label: Require Liveness Check
fields.description: Kiosks ask the person to turn their head or smile before matching, to make a held-up photo harder. The check runs on the phone, so the server cannot verify it. Turn it off only for testing.

fields.label: Match Margin
fields.description: At a kiosk the app searches all employees. The best match must beat the second-best by at least this much, otherwise the scan is refused as ambiguous. Higher values reduce look-alike mix-ups but reject more scans. Default 0.05.

fields.label: Return To Camera After (seconds)
fields.description: After a successful check-in the kiosk shows the result for this many seconds, then returns to the camera for the next person.

fields.label: Allow PIN Attendance
fields.description: Lets employees who have a PIN mark attendance from the kiosk keypad when face recognition fails. Turning it off hides the keypad on every kiosk. PINs are set and reset by HR only.

fields.label: Minimum PIN Length
fields.description: Shortest PIN HR may set, in digits. Easy PINs such as 1234 or 1111 are always refused.

fields.label: Maximum PIN Length
fields.description: Longest PIN HR may set, in digits. Keep it at or above the minimum.

fields.label: Keep Proof Photos (days)
fields.description: A PIN check-in saves the kiosk camera photo on the Employee Checkin as proof of who was there. Photos older than this many days are deleted automatically each day; the check-in record itself stays. Face check-ins save no photo.

fields.label: Allow Offline Attendance
fields.description: When a kiosk cannot reach the server, it saves each face scan on the phone, encrypted, and sends it later. The server then works out who it was; the phone never decides. Each kiosk must also be switched on by HR under Biometric Device.

fields.label: Offline Window (hours)
fields.description: How long a scan may wait on the phone. A scan older than this when it arrives, or taken after the phone restarted, is held for HR to review instead of becoming a check-in.

fields.label: Clock Tolerance (minutes)
fields.description: How far the phone's own clock may differ from the time worked out from the last server contact before the scan is held for HR. Catches a clock that was changed.

fields.label: Review Window (days)
fields.description: A held offline scan that HR has not approved or rejected within this many days is closed as rejected, with a note. Nothing is deleted.
